name: Simon Hamui Space
about: Furniture showroom in Aspen lined in pale poplar boards under a slatted ceiling, staged with the studio's own stone and timber pieces.
notes: An interior (a showroom), not a building. Surface: the poplar slat ceiling (photo 03); the carved panels in 03 and 10 are an artwork by César Núñez, not a finish.

name: Casa Kakmo
about: Renovated house and guest house in Izamal, Yucatán's 'Yellow City', with white and Izamal-yellow walls along a long narrow pool.
notes: Interiors by Dórica Arquitectura. Surface: the yellow-washed plaster wall (photo 01); plaster read from the photo.

name: Armani 3400
about: Tone-on-tone oceanfront apartment interior with curved white sofas, oak-veneer slat walls, veined marble and a spa-like palette.
notes: Interior project (credits: interior designer FL Interiors with Lacruz Design Studio). Surface: the striated grey stone of the shower wall (photo 12), seen through glass so slightly soft. The veined marble around the TV (photo 10) was too narrow between the TV and the slats to crop at 25% of the short side.

name: Three Gardens House
about: Family house in Kuwait built round three gardens stacked for the heat: a sunken summer garden, a pool courtyard and a roof garden under aluminium mesh, behind a plain stone front.
notes: No year in the article. Hero 01: the stone-clad street front with the cantilevered volumes and the mesh skin. Surface: the reflective white ceramic tile, laid in herringbone, that lines the inner courtyard (photo 10). Mesh is the anodised aluminium deploye the article describes. sustainable-design: the whole plan is a passive response to the climate.

name: Minnesota Residence
about: A lakeside family house in Minnesota stepping down a wooded slope to a dock, its open rooms joined by one run of wide white-oak planks.
notes: No architect is named: the byline 'by RIVA Spain' is the flooring maker (credits: Flooring Riva Spain, with Unique Wood Floors), so architect is null; no town given. Surface = the veined stone kitchen island (the article says 'stone'; it looks like marble).

name: Casa Sisal
about: Low white guest house on the old henequen drying fields of Hacienda Sac Chich, between a lily pond and an infinity pool, finished in Mayan chukum plaster.
notes: Architect from the credits ('Reyes Ríos + Larraín Arquitectos'; og:title drops the accents and 'Arquitectos'). Surface: the mottled cream chukum-type finish of the terrace floor (photo 09). The article names chukum for the walls; the floor shows the same finish. The walls in photo 04 are in perspective and could not be cropped square at 25%.

name: Lardero Chalet
about: Interior renovation of a white cubic suburban chalet with a pool, oak floors, timber slat screens and a marble-look ceramic slab as a headboard wall.
notes: Name from og:title (the raw name 'Transforming a Residential Chalet' is the article headline). Credits name the interior designer 'Nájera y Boto'; og:title's fuller studio name used. The article calls the colours vibrant, but the photos are mostly white and oak with a few coloured pieces, so no colour gene. Surface: the large-format ceramic slab behind the bed (photo 18), left of its fluted section.

name: Strazik House
about: Long low house of pigmented concrete and local stone laid across a vineyard in the Uco Valley, facing the Andes.
notes: AA says Mendoza; the article places it in Los Chacayes, Tunuyán. Surface: board-formed pigmented concrete of the fireplace wall (photo 06).

name: Living N5 on the CASA FOA Platform
about: Show-house living room at CASA FOA Córdoba, wood on every wall, floor and ceiling, furnished in greens around an indoor garden.
notes: An interior installation, not a building. Architect is the AA byline (the furniture maker); credits list Patricio Calderón Rojas as architect and Estudio Ache__O as interior designer. Surface: the green Avocatus quartzite (photo 09).

name: Ca na Joaneta
about: Century-old rubble-stone farmhouse in the Pla de Mallorca, rebuilt as an off-grid family retreat with a timber mezzanine inside.
notes: Architect spelled as in the article credits (og:title has the typo Different Desing). AA says Palma; the article places it between Ariany and Maria de la Salut. Ceramic = the clay roof tiles. Surface: the local stone masonry wall (photo 05).

name: Dacha Retreat
about: Compact timber tower in the forest near Chillán, clad in charred pine and lined with local lingue slats, joined to the slope by a single bridge on the upper floor.
notes: Architect as the article title gives it (DRAA); the text itself says the design was "crafted by Aguilo + Pedraza Arquitectos". No year in the article. Hero 05: the dark tower and its bridge in daylight. Surface: the charred pine boards (photo 10, right of the upper window). Concrete: the plinth under the tower in photo 10. sustainable-design: the article is about heat storage and efficiency.

name: Casa BP
about: Long, nearly windowless volume in red pigmented render on a rural slope near Córdoba, open on one side to a timber gallery and a linear pool.
notes: Year null: the article gives none. residential/projects says 2024, but that is not from the article. 'plaster' = the article's 'pigmented cement render with a handcrafted texture'; 'steel' = the pavilion's black metal joinery. Surface: the mottled, hand-trowelled red render of the blind wall, between the two scuppers (photo 03). Photo 08 shows it too, but with branches across it.

name: Casa Homenaje
about: Two-storey house outside Gijón made of white cantilevered slabs and long glazing, with timber panels set between them and gardens on several levels.
notes: No year in the article. Hero 08: the garden front, white bands and timber panels. Surface: the vertical timber cladding boards (photo 09, right). Materials are the ones the article names (wood, steel, glass); the white walls are not named.

name: La Providencia Residence
about: Two-storey grey-and-white box house on a slope near Gijón, with oak floors, a glass-railed stair and walls of glass onto the garden.
notes: Credits name the architect Veronica Duran Sela. Surface: light oak plank floor (photo 06).

name: Neuendorf House
about: Holiday house on Mallorca made of walls of rust-pink lime stucco, reached along a long straight stone path and set beside a 30 m pool.
notes: Year null: the article gives no date (residential/projects says 1989, not from the article). AA says Palma; the projects file says near Santanyi. Surface: sunlit patch of the hand-finished lime stucco wall (photo 07).

name: Casa Berman
about: Two-storey exposed-concrete house in Buenos Aires built around a patio, with breeze-block screens and an open ground floor.
notes: og:title's 'Arquitectos' used (credits write 'ARQuitectos'). The article names no materials; all four are from the photos (exposed concrete slabs, concrete blocks and breeze-blocks, glass, timber, steel stair). Surface: the concrete breeze-block screen by the patio (photo 10), with the garden showing through.

name: UNPUENTE
about: Lakeside family house above Embalse Los Molinos, entered from the street across a curving timber-railed bridge, with rubble-stone walls, exposed concrete and a helical stair under a skylight.
notes: No year in the article. Hero 08: the curving entrance bridge past the stone wall, the idea the house is named for. Surface: the sunlit rubble stone of that same wall (photo 08, top left), so hero and surface share a photo. Materials: the article names exposed concrete, iron and wood; the stone walls are what the photos show most.

name: Anantara Mina Al Arab Ras Al Khaimah Resort
about: Beach resort on a private peninsula in Ras Al Khaimah whose thatched villas stand on stilts over the sea, reached by curving boardwalks.
notes: Architect as the article title gives it: Anantara Hotels and Resorts is the hotel group, the article names no designer. No year in the article. Hero 02: one overwater villa, reads at phone size (08, the aerial ring of villas, is the alternative). Surface: veined white marble floor of a villa bathroom (photo 06); a small triangle of the timber door shows in the top-right corner, the only clean marble patch big enough. Materials: thatch roofs are visible too but have no deck word.

name: Casa en el Dragon
about: Hillside house in the Córdoba sierras made of board-marked concrete slabs cantilevered over a stone base, its long glazed rooms and galleries facing the valley.
notes: No year in the article. Hero 05: the cantilevered concrete slabs over the stone base. Surface: the board-formed concrete wall of the stair hall (photo 11). The text speaks of "mineral renders"; the photos show board-formed concrete throughout, so concrete is listed.

name: Las Casuarinas
about: Hillside house in Lima furnished by an interior studio in soft neutrals with black accents, warm timber and large indoor plants.
notes: The article says interior design is the main subject, so the hero is the living room (04), not the exterior (01). Surface: the grey cleft-stone paving of the pool courtyard (photo 13), to use as a floor.

name: Casa CM
about: Corner house in Río Ceballos on a raised podium: an L of board-marked concrete below, a closed white box above with aluminium sunshades to the north, round a pool patio.
notes: No year in the article. Hero 04: the white box overhanging the concrete base. Surface: the board-formed concrete of the stair wall (photo 10, left; slight perspective). The white upper box material is not named, so it is not listed.

name: Marlborough Residence
about: A white Mediterranean-style family house in West Palm Beach with arches and columns, held together by dark European-oak floors and a stone floor inlaid with bands of wood at the entry.
notes: No architect is named: the byline 'by RIVA Spain' is the flooring maker (credits: Flooring Riva Spain, Builder Counihan Construction), so architect is null. 'ceramic' = the terracotta roof tiles (photo), 'iron' = the stair balustrade (article).

name: Justiniano Building
about: Apartment block in Córdoba with a gridded exposed-concrete street front whose slab ceilings carry on out to the balconies.
notes: Surface: the mottled exposed-concrete ceiling with formwork joints (photo 06). Stone = granite counter and grey floor tiles, from the photos.

name: The Hotel Azur Lobby
about: A hotel lobby built as the centrepiece of a design fair in Córdoba, a 12 m tall hall split into small rooms: a ring of hanging glazed tiles round a raw stone, round banquettes under plants, a lit wall of room keys.
notes: An interior installation, not a building; Interior Designer Estudio Montevideo. No year in the article. Hero 01: the cylinder of hanging tiles in the lobby. Surface: the curtain of hanging glazed ceramic tiles (photo 08; Almagre Ceramicas is credited). Materials are the article's (timber, local stone, felt, stucco) plus the ceramic seen. grid: the backlit key wall (photo 16).

name: Pabellon Polideportivo Carlos Soria
about: Municipal sports hall in Ávila built from one humble local hollow brick, topped with a translucent polycarbonate box and bolted galvanized-steel trusses.
notes: 'brick' is not a deck material word (ceramic would hide what it is); 'plastic' is polycarbonate, as build_deck maps it. Surface: the brick wall (photo 15).

name: Clínica Dental Vega
about: Dental clinic in an old building in central Salamanca: oak panelling and slatted screens, sand tones after the city's stone, and a central block of treatment rooms laid out on Campaspero stone sizes.
notes: An interior fit-out. No year in the article. Hero 01: the waiting area with the oak slat screen and panelled wall. Surface: the oak veneer of a panelled door (photo 07, below the vision panel). Stone: the Campaspero stone column and base (photos 06, 07).

name: Naman Pure Spa
about: An open-air spa at a Da Nang resort behind a white lattice of vertical fins hung with gardens, where sunlight falls in moving patches across pale walls and floors.
notes: Surface = a finely fluted white wall in dappled light. Article: 'locally sourced wood and stone'.

name: Escala Humana Wines Winery
architect: Estudio Monte Arquitectura, Estudio RARE and Unamuno Arquitectura
about: Family winery in Gualtallary, Mendoza: a long low barn of thick local stone walls under a dark pitched metal roof, opening west to the Andes, with concrete eggs and amphorae inside.
notes: Year 2024: the article says "Completed in 2024" (2015 is when the winery was founded). Hero 06: the stone barn against the snowy Andes. Surface null: the river-stone wall is the material, but no photo shows it at 25% of the short side; the best is photo 04, crop [0.08, 0.69, 0.14, 0.21] (358 px, 21%), clean and usable if the rule is relaxed. "metal" is the article's word for the roof, kept plain.

name: The Alfa Collection
about: A pitcher, infuser and coffee pot in raw unglazed stoneware with hardwood handles and aluminium lids, from a ceramics studio near Córdoba.
notes: NOT A BUILDING: the article is about three ceramic objects, so this fits the OBJECT kind better than SPACE. Verify made it an object card (kind 'object', category Design/Decorative Art, as Artsy files design objects) and moved the surface crop inside the pitcher's body. Hero 03 (the pitcher pouring) says what it is. If a space picture is needed, photo 08 shows the exhibition room it was shown in, which the article does not describe. Credits: 'Artist'. Surface: the speckled unglazed stoneware body (photo 03), as a clay or tile finish. 'sustainable-design' for the local clay and the reused Guayubira wood.

name: Allison Island Residence
about: A Mediterranean-style villa on Miami Beach's Allison Island whose white, gallery-like interiors, sculptural stair and gold-veined marble kitchen sit on honey-toned wide oak planks.
notes: No architect is named: the byline 'by RIVA Spain' is the flooring maker (credits: Flooring Riva Spain, General Contractor NAFA Construction, Products Madera Studio), so architect is null. Hero is the curved stair, since the article's point is the interior. Surface = the oak floor (RIVA's Krypton).

name: Suspended Stone Houses
about: Two houses in the hills of Yacanto, Córdoba, whose walls of stone taken from the site ride on cantilevered concrete slabs, so they seem to hover over the slope.
notes: Surface = the site-stone cladding.

name: Woodsong
about: Alfred Browning Parker's timber house in a Coconut Grove jungle garden, with a pool running in under wood ceilings and round oculi.
notes: Year null: the article only says 'mid-20th century'. 'mid-century-modern-design' is a real Artsy gene, but its family (Design Movements) is not one the deck keeps, so it is not used. Hero 03 (pool under the oculus and timber ceiling) rather than the dusk exterior (08), which is mostly palms at small size. Surface: vertical tongue-and-groove wall boards (photo 04), at exactly 25% of the short side.

name: Casa YB
about: Square courtyard house among orchards in Maule, Chile: glazed timber galleries around a clay-tiled patio ringed by a strip of water.
notes: Credits: Augusto Domínguez Ruiz-Tagle. Surface: sunlit timber gallery floor (photo 06); the clay-tile patio, the main material in the text, is never shown flat and large enough to crop.

name: Centro Cultural Los Lavaderos
about: Three-storey brick cultural centre in Zaratán built over the town's old stone washhouses, which stay visible under glass floors.
notes: og:title for this one is a different headline ('...: Heritage and Community'); the name comes from the page title. 'concrete' is from the credited precast structure (Rubiera Prefabricados), 'stone' is the preserved washhouse. Surface: the pale exposed brick in the stair hall (photo 07).

name: Residence Oliva
about: House in Mendiolaza, Córdoba, of exposed concrete planes and a dark box on a stone-clad base, with deep eaves, low strip windows and a timber-lined gallery by the pool.
notes: No year in the article. Hero 02: the concrete volumes and the dark box. Surface: the timber board ceiling of the gallery (photo 10). The exposed concrete is the article's main material, but no sharp concrete patch reaches 25% of a photo's short side (photo 02's wall band is about 20%; the soffit in photo 04 is out of focus). Steel: the rusted weathering-steel boxes seen in photos 02 and 04 (not named in the text).

name: El Vasco Boulevard
about: A 120,000 m² mixed-use complex in Oviedo (shops, restaurants, cinemas, sport) strung along a raised pedestrian boulevard, its blocks clad in pale stone panels.
notes: Credits spell the name without accents ('Veronica Duran Sela'); og:title's accented form used. Materials from the photos (the article names none).

name: Medika 10
about: Medical and commercial complex in Guatemala City whose central lobby is roofed by a field of 24 differently angled skylight boxes.
notes: Hero is the skylight lobby, which the article calls the defining feature, not the street front (01). Architect spelled as in the article text (og:title drops the accent). Surface: wall of rust-patinated steel tube sections (photo 07); steel and the grey stone floor are read from the photos, the article names no materials.

name: Studio Fran Viñas Arquitectos
about: Narrow architects' studio in Córdoba: a tall prism veiled in perforated metal, entered through a bright red box doorway, with a red spiral stair inside.
notes: The article says 'perforated metal'; aluminium is inferred from the credits (Aluar, Hunter Douglas). Surface: the ribbed perforated metal screen (photo 08).

name: Casa Galera
about: Single-storey house in Río Tercero that spans its lot behind a timber-slatted street front and opens onto a garden courtyard and pool.
notes: Surface: board-formed concrete ceiling with wood grain (photo 08).

name: The Villa in La Quinta
about: Three-level white villa on a Tenerife cliff, built of basalt, concrete and wood, with infinity pools and a spiral stair wound around an olive tree.
notes: Name as the article writes it (raw name: The Villa). Surface: squared volcanic stone blocks lining the indoor pond, seen through the water (photo 07); photo 10 shows the rough basalt better but the wall is too narrow to crop.

name: Valpo 1
about: Row of brick loft houses on the edge of Córdoba, each with a double-height kitchen behind a perforated brick lattice.
notes: The article (which repeats two paragraphs) calls the scheme 'Valpo Lofts'. 'glass' is visible and Saint-Gobain Glass is credited. Surface: the solid-and-perforated brick wall of unit 4 (photo 07), straight on.

name: Casa S
about: A calm Buenos Aires house of pale painted-brick planes and deep covered terraces, its living spaces opening onto a garden and pool.
notes: Surface = the vein-cut travertine fireplace wall (looks travertine; the article says only 'mineral and concrete-based surfaces'). Brick and stone from the photos.

name: Casa La Flecha
about: A music room added to a house above the Río de la Plata: a concrete floor plane and a timber-lined roof held apart by a slim frame, open to the river.
notes: og:title adds 'and Eduardo Vera', whom the credits list for landscape and interior design; the credited architect is used. The article is about the music room addition; hero is its interior with the piano and the river. Surface = weathered exposed concrete (the article expects it to age).

name: Casa R&C
about: A Córdoba house in two parts: a heavy cyclopean-concrete base studded with stones, and an upper floor under five exposed-brick vaults, with the water tank in a separate concrete tower.
notes: Surface = the cyclopean concrete wall with stone inclusions (article: 'cyclopean concrete … natural stone inclusions'). 'brick' is a plain word: the deck has no brick material.

name: Rue Jean-Bart
about: Paris apartment infill whose local limestone front swells into rows of scalloped balcony curves on the upper floors.
notes: No date in the article. Surface: the honed Vassens limestone blocks beside the entrance (photo 16), with the joints and a niche edge showing. 'sustainable-design' for the article's local-quarry sourcing and Paris climate-plan performance.

name: Depart Colegiales
about: An apartment building in Colegiales, Buenos Aires, facing a new railway park: stacked bands of exposed concrete, timber shutters, planted terraces and a shop-lined ground floor.
notes: AA files this housing block as Commercial (kept as use). City empty in the bookmark; Colegiales is a Buenos Aires neighbourhood. Surface = the oak floor of a bedroom (photo 21); Verify moved it from the timber shutters (photo 20), whose square also took in a concrete band and glass.

name: Casa VCH
about: Three-level family house in La Moraleja, Madrid: pale stone-faced boxes, concrete walls and timber louvres, entered past a water feature and set round patios, garden and pool.
notes: No year in the article. Hero 01: the house over the pool at dusk. Surface: the large grey block wall beside the entrance path (photo 02, right; slight perspective). The article calls the material concrete; Bateig (a stone quarry) is credited, so stone is listed too. The warm slab wall of photo 10 was the other candidate, but the evening light colours it brown.

name: Vista Clara House
about: Art collectors' house in Cholula whose entrance is a black-marble frame around full-height glass, with reflecting pools, timber panelling and a floating stair inside.
notes: Name from og:title (raw name had 'Modern Elegance' attached). Credits say 'Cibrian Arquitectos'; og:title's 'Fernando Cibrian' kept. 'steel' is the metal lattice on the living-room wall and ceiling the article names. Onyx is named too and left out (no deck word closer than stone). Surface: polished black marble with white veins (photo 04).

name: The UC Innovation Center
about: A monolithic concrete tower for research and start-ups on a Santiago campus, with deep-set openings in an opaque skin and a glass atrium where the usual core would be.
notes: Credits write 'Elemental'; og:title's 'ELEMENTAL' used. Surface = board-marked exposed concrete.

name: Pre-Columbian Museum
about: Renovation of Santiago's Chilean Museum of Pre-Columbian Art that adds dark underground galleries and a charcoal concrete stair inside the white colonial building.
notes: AA files it as Commercial though it is a museum. The article names no materials: dark concrete and white plaster are read from the photos. Surface: charcoal concrete of the stair (photo 07).

name: Finca Aguy
about: A prefabricated timber cabin of two factory-built 12.5 m modules, set on low dry-stone walls in an olive grove near Pueblo Edén.
notes: Surface = the board-lined (pine-looking) interior wall; the article says only 'timber-clad interior'.

name: Miami Residence
about: 1,500 m² family house in Miami reworked as a 'contemporary farmhouse', wrapped inside in wood panelling around a symmetrical plan.
notes: Year 2024 from the article ('Completed in late 2024'). Hero is the wood-panelled kitchen and dining room (01): the panelling is the point, and the exterior (20) reads small. Linen curtains and cotton rugs are named in the article. 'stone' is the marble or quartzite island and the backsplashes in the photos. Surface: walnut-tone veneer panels (photo 05), away from the person in the frame.

name: Casa LL
about: House of blind, earth-tinted concrete blocks at the foot of the Tepozteco cliffs, closed to the street and opening onto a garden.
notes: og:title's 'RA! Arquitectura' (credits just 'RA!'). The structure is EPS panels with wire mesh under tinted concrete; mapped to 'concrete'. Surface: the tinted concrete wall straight on, with its horizontal formwork lines (photo 03, the same photo as the hero).

name: Balboa
about: Hilltop house in Del Mar, California, with glass walls onto terraces and the Pacific, floored throughout in wide hand-finished oak planks.
notes: Architect as the article title gives it: RIVA Spain made the oak floors; the article is about the floors and names no architect for the house. No year in the article. Hero 05: the open living and dining room with the oak floor and the view. Surface: the oak planks (photo 05, bottom right, left of the rug).

name: Llagar Renovation
about: A ruined stone cider mill near the Asturian coast made into a two-storey house: the old rubble walls hold a new box of timber, steel and glass, with timber boarding above the stone.
notes: No year in the article. Hero 04: the gable end, rubble stone below and timber above. Surface: the rubble sandstone masonry of that gable (photo 04, below the window line). patterns: the patterned floor tiles inside (photos 08-11). time: the article makes time "another material of the project".

name: Cavendish Housing
about: Row of houses in Córdoba, Argentina: white, finely ribbed upper boxes over slanted walls of timber slats, with skylit white stair halls inside.
notes: No year in the article. Hero 10: the row of units, which says "housing" better than a single front. Surface: the timber slat wall (photo 03; two hidden-door hinges show). Plaster stands for the "rendered surfaces" the article names; the dark frames are only "metal", so no metal is listed.

name: The Headquarters of BEEAH Group
about: Headquarters for an environmental-services company in Sharjah: a run of linked, dune-like white shells, pierced inside by lattices of light under a ventilating dome.
notes: og:title spells the firm 'Zaha Hadid Architect'; the article's credits say 'Zaha Hadid Architects', used here. The article names no materials: 'concrete' is the glass-fibre-reinforced concrete (GRC) cladding named on zaha-hadid.com and in the CIBSE facade-award write-up, 'glass' is visible. Surface = the perforated auditorium ceiling.

name: Casa Conlon
about: 1,300 m² hacienda-style house on the Sea of Cortez with dark timber beams, rough stone walls, antique carved doors and vaulted plaster ceilings.
notes: Credits spell 'Paulina Jiménez' (og:title drops the accent). She is credited as interior designer; the article names no architect. Surface: the irregular stacked-stone wall by the fireplace (photo 02). The carved antique doors in photo 15 were the alternative, but stone is easier to use as a wall.

name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
about: Tribute to Frank Gehry, architect of folded stainless-steel and titanium landmarks; the card shows his Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles.
notes: Not one building: an obituary covering many works. Hero and surface use photo 02, Walt Disney Concert Hall (opened 2003, per the article). Verify named the card after the building it shows (Walt Disney Concert Hall, 2003) rather than the obituary's title 'Frank Gehry 1929–2025'.

name: Casa Cosmo
about: Board-formed concrete polyhedron on a rammed-stone plinth in the Córdoba hills, hollowed inside like a cave and lit by a triangular skylight.
notes: Steel = expanded-metal sliding shutters. Surface: river stones set in the board-marked plinth wall (photo 14).

name: Le Cèdre Socio-Cultural Center
about: A community and youth centre for a renewed Asnières neighbourhood: a prefabricated spruce and Douglas-fir frame wrapped in white brick under sloping zinc roofs, set around preserved cedars.
notes: Raw name was 'The Le Cèdre…'; og:title's 'Le Cèdre Socio-Cultural Center' used. City not in the bookmark: the article places it in the Hauts d'Asnières district, i.e. Asnières-sur-Seine. AA files it as Commercial though it is a civic building. 'brick' and 'zinc' are plain words: the deck has no brick or zinc material.

name: Clinica Dental Apolonia
about: Dental clinic in Valladolid shaped by curves: walls bend into the ceiling in sand-textured paint under indirect light, with an oak and stone-look reception desk.
notes: An interior fit-out. No year in the article. Hero 05: the curved wall running into the ceiling at reception. Surface: the sand-textured paint of a curved wall (photo 04); the texture is soft, a warm beige wall colour more than a pattern. Materials are the article's own words (textured paint with natural sand, natural wood), so "paint" and "sand" are plain words, not deck words.

name: The Ranch at El Paraiso
about: A five-acre family estate in an equestrian community west of Delray Beach: ranch-house gables with aluminium barn doors and shutters, cypress beams and a poured-concrete frame.
notes: Byline 'by Paterson Project Management' is the builder; the credits name the architect, Bruce Celenski (used). Raw name 'A Five-Acre Equestrian Estate' came from the headline; og:title's name used. Year: 'Completed in April 2026'. Hero is a white board-sided gable with red barn doors (the main house or its barn: the article does not say which). Surface = the patterned engineered-wood floor.

name: University of Jyväskylä Campus
about: Alvar Aalto's red-brick university buildings set in a horseshoe around a sports field, with white skylit halls and stairs inside.
notes: Year null: the only year in the article, 1992, is when the complex was protected by law, not when it was completed. AA files a university under 'Commercial'; kept as AA's category. Granite is named and mapped to 'stone'. Surface: a straight-on run of the red brick wall under the skylights (photo 08). 'mid-century-modern-design' is a real Artsy gene but its family is Design Movements, which the deck does not keep, so it is not used.

name: Residence 204
about: A long, low house in Córdoba planned around a carob tree it kept, with local stone walls, exposed concrete and a deep timber-lined roof over the garden.
notes: Surface = the local stone wall of the entrance hall (crop includes a small vent and a switch box).

name: Pueblo Serena
about: A Monterrey shopping centre laid out like a Mexican village around a church, with dry-stacked stone walls, timber eaves, lattice screens and planted plazas.
notes: Hero shows the white church tower beside a stacked-stone pier. Surface = dry-stacked flagstone wall. Materials from the photos (the article names none).
